metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with a deployable HTTP entry point (index.cfm and download.cfm are IIS-served CFML pages with an <cfapplication> bootstrap) scoped to a single service. No sibling service directories, and the pages are deployed rather than published as a package, so monorepo and library do not apply.
metadata.archetype_justification: Both pages are read-only database queries over dbo.documents with free-text search and sort (index.cfm) and a single-row lookup plus file stream (download.cfm). Logic is dominated by query-and-serialize with no write endpoints, no message consumers and no downstream service fan-out.

tech_stack.framework: Adobe ColdFusion 8 on IIS 7 (no application framework; <cfapplication> session management)
tech_stack.architecture: Single-instance server-rendered page monolith on Windows Server 2008; SQL Server 2005 metadata store; document bytes on local disk (D:\docroot\files); manual file-copy deployment

findings.title: Documented API Interface
findings.description: The repository contains only two server-rendered CFML pages. index.cfm emits an HTML table of documents and download.cfm streams a file with <cfcontent>. No REST, GraphQL, gRPC or AsyncAPI surface exists: searched for *.graphql/*.gql, openapi.*/swagger.*, *.smithy, AsyncAPI specs, and for any CFC component or remote-method declaration (access="remote", <cfcomponent>, <cffunction returnformat="json">) across all 4 repository files — zero results. The only machine-consumable integration paths are HTML scraping of index.cfm or direct SQL Server access to the docportal datasource.
findings.gap: There is no programmatic API for an agent to bind to. Integration would require UI scraping of HTML generated by index.cfm (fragile, non-auditable) or direct database access that bypasses the application's session check entirely.
findings.recommendation: Expose the document search and retrieval operations behind an HTTP JSON API — either by adding ColdFusion remote CFCs (access="remote", returnformat="json") in front of the existing queries as a tactical step, or preferably by extracting the document search/download operations into a supported runtime fronted by API Gateway. Publish an OpenAPI description of that surface (see API-Q2).

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No machine-readable interface description exists. Searched for openapi.yaml/json, swagger.yaml/json, AsyncAPI documents, *.graphql/*.gql and *.smithy across the repository; the only files present are README.md, index.cfm, download.cfm and .gitignore. No dependency manifest exists that could declare a spec-generation toolchain.
findings.gap: No OpenAPI/GraphQL/Smithy artifact, so agent tool definitions cannot be generated and would have to be hand-authored against scraped HTML.
findings.recommendation: Once an API surface exists (API-Q1), publish and version an OpenAPI 3.x document for the document search and download operations, generated from the implementation rather than hand-maintained, and validate it in CI.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No error handling exists in either page. download.cfm interpolates url.id directly into SQL (line 4) and passes doc.filename into <cfcontent file="#filepath#">; a missing id, a non-numeric id or a missing file on D:\docroot\files yields an unhandled ColdFusion exception page. There is no <cftry>/<cfcatch>, no <cferror>, no onError handler, and no Application.cfc. Failure is communicated as an HTML ColdFusion error page, not a structured body.
findings.gap: Callers receive HTML stack-trace pages rather than machine-readable error codes, so an agent cannot distinguish a retriable fault (database unavailable) from a terminal one (document id not found, file missing on disk).
findings.recommendation: Add an Application.cfc onError handler and <cftry>/<cfcatch> around both queries and the file-streaming call, returning a consistent JSON error envelope with an error code, message and retryable flag; map not-found, invalid-input and backend-failure to distinct codes.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: No write endpoints exist in the repository. index.cfm performs a single SELECT and download.cfm performs a SELECT plus a read-only file stream (deletefile="no"). The README documents an upload feature ("Uploaded files written to local disk with original filenames"), but no upload handler is present in the repository, so no write path can be assessed here. agent_scope resolved to read-only, so idempotency is informational.
findings.gap: Idempotency cannot be evaluated because no write surface is present. If the documented upload handler is added to this repository later, it will need idempotency keys or a unique business key before any write-enabled agent is pointed at it.
findings.recommendation: When the upload path is brought into this repository or rebuilt, require a client-supplied idempotency key and enforce a unique constraint on (filename, uploaded_by, content hash) so a retried upload cannot create duplicate document rows.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: agent_scope=read-only (has_write_operations=false — only SELECT queries and a read-only file stream are present).
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: No POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE or state-mutating handler exists in index.cfm or download.cfm, so an integrated agent has no write path to retry against.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are server-rendered HTML (index.cfm emits an HTML <table> via <cfoutput query="docs">) and raw binary (download.cfm sets Content-Disposition: attachment and <cfcontent type="application/octet-stream">). No JSON or XML serialization appears anywhere; no returnformat="json" declarations exist.
findings.gap: HTML-plus-binary responses are not directly consumable as agent tool output. An agent would need an HTML parser tightly coupled to the current table markup, which breaks on any presentation change.
findings.recommendation: Return JSON for document metadata and keep binary streaming only for the document bytes themselves, with the content type and filename carried in structured metadata rather than inferred from headers.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limiting or throttling of any kind was found: there is no IaC (no API Gateway usage plan, no WAF rate rule), no reverse-proxy configuration in the repository, and no application-level throttling in index.cfm or download.cfm. No X-RateLimit-* or Retry-After headers are emitted — the only <cfheader> call sets Content-Disposition. The README states the application runs on a single IIS 7 instance.
findings.gap: Limits are neither enforced nor advertised, so an agent cannot self-throttle and has no signal when it is overloading the single instance.
findings.recommendation: When the API surface is introduced, place it behind a gateway that enforces a per-caller usage plan and returns X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After headers, and document the limits alongside the OpenAPI spec.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: Authentication is entirely human-session based. index.cfm declares <cfapplication sessionmanagement="yes" sessiontimeout="30 min"> and gates access with structKeyExists(session, "userid"), redirecting to login.cfm when absent. There is no OAuth2 client-credentials flow, no API key handling, no mTLS configuration, no service-account definition and no gateway authorizer anywhere in the repository; the README confirms "Application-managed sessions, no SSO". download.cfm performs no authentication check at all — it will stream any document to any unauthenticated caller that knows a doc_id.
findings.gap: There is no way for a non-human caller to authenticate as itself, and therefore no authenticated principal that could be attributed to an agent in any log. An agent could only integrate by replaying a human user's session cookie, which destroys attribution and inherits that human's full access.
findings.recommendation: Introduce machine identity before any agent integration: front the new API surface (API-Q1) with an identity provider issuing per-agent client credentials (OAuth 2.0 client-credentials or a gateway authorizer with per-key principal attribution), require the authenticated principal on every request including the download path, and carry that principal into the audit record (AUTH-Q6).

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: Authorization is a single binary gate: index.cfm checks only whether session.userid exists, and every authenticated session sees the same unfiltered document list (the <cfquery> on lines 22-28 filters only on the title search term, never on the caller). download.cfm has no check whatsoever. There are no roles, groups, scopes or permission tables, and no IaC with IAM policies. All database access flows through the single shared "docportal" datasource.
findings.gap: The authorization model offers no mechanism to scope a caller down — a document-reading agent would necessarily receive the same access as every human user, across every document category, with unbounded blast radius.
findings.recommendation: Add a permission model keyed on the caller principal (minimum: per-category or per-document-owner access rules enforced inside the query predicate) so an agent identity can be granted access to a narrow document subset, and enforce it in both the listing and the download path.

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The only check in the codebase is the session-existence test in index.cfm lines 5-7; there are no canRead/canWrite/canDelete style checks, no RBAC or ABAC policy definitions, no permission matrix, and no per-operation gating. Access to download.cfm is not distinguished from access to the listing page in any way.
findings.gap: The system cannot grant read without implicitly granting whatever other operations the application exposes (including the upload path documented in the README), so an agent's capability set cannot be constrained by action.
findings.recommendation: Define explicit operations (searchDocuments, downloadDocument, uploadDocument) and authorize each one separately against the caller principal, so a read-only agent identity is structurally incapable of invoking the write operations.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: No identity propagation mechanism exists: no JWT parsing, no OAuth token exchange, no on-behalf-of flow and no X-User-Id style header handling. Identity lives only in the ColdFusion session scope (session.userid, session.fullname in index.cfm) and is never carried onward — the sole downstream call is the <cfquery> to the shared docportal datasource, which connects with a single static credential regardless of the user. Severity downgraded to INFO per archetype calibration for data-gateway services.
findings.gap: An agent could not act on behalf of a specific user with that user's bounded permissions; it would either replay the user's session wholesale or connect as the shared datasource identity. Because the detected archetype is a read-only document query layer, this is recorded as an architecture input rather than a safety risk.
findings.recommendation: If an on-behalf-of agent workflow is planned, add token-based identity to the new API surface and distinguish agent-as-self from agent-for-user in both the authorization predicate and the audit record.

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: Database credentials are managed outside version control in the ColdFusion Administrator datasource definition (<cfquery datasource="docportal"> in both index.cfm and download.cfm references it by name), with no secrets manager and no rotation. The README discloses the administrator password in plaintext: "Datasource credentials configured in CF Administrator, password is 'cfadmin'". No aws_secretsmanager_* resources, Vault client, or .env file exist (.gitignore does exclude .env and .env.*).
findings.gap: A weak, documented, never-rotated administrator credential is recorded in the repository itself. Any caller — including an agent with access to repository content or to the README — can read it, and there is no rotation path that would limit the exposure window.
findings.recommendation: Rotate the ColdFusion Administrator password immediately and remove the plaintext value from README.md and from git history. Move the datasource credential into a managed secret store with scheduled rotation, and grant the application a least-privilege SQL login (SELECT on dbo.documents only) rather than an administrative one.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. Neither index.cfm nor download.cfm writes any log record — there is no <cflog>, no Application.cfc, no CloudTrail or CloudWatch configuration (no IaC of any kind), and no immutable or tamper-evident log storage. Document retrievals through download.cfm leave no trace of who retrieved which document. agent_scope resolved to read-only, so this is RISK-SAFETY rather than BLOCKER.
findings.gap: There is no record attributing any access to a principal, so agent-initiated document retrievals would be indistinguishable from human ones and entirely invisible after the fact — forensics on a document exfiltration would be impossible.
findings.recommendation: Emit a structured access log for every search and download containing the authenticated principal (AUTH-Q1), the document id, the timestamp and the caller type, and ship it to append-only storage with retention and integrity validation enabled.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only (has_write_operations=false), so the conditional BLOCKER resolves to its read-only severity.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The repository exposes no write operations, so audit attribution gaps affect read traceability and exfiltration forensics rather than unprovable state mutation; has_auth_surface is true (session gate in index.cfm), so the question is evaluated rather than downgraded to INFO.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: There is no identity to suspend and no mechanism to suspend one. The repository contains no API key store, no credential revocation endpoint, no service-account disable path and no IAM/Cognito configuration. The only revocation primitive implied by the code is ColdFusion session expiry (sessiontimeout 30 minutes in index.cfm line 3), which is time-based and cannot be targeted at a single misbehaving caller.
findings.gap: A misbehaving integration could only be stopped by taking the application offline or by changing the shared datasource credential — both of which disrupt every user. Per-identity isolation is not possible.
findings.recommendation: Issue per-agent credentials through an identity provider that supports immediate revocation, and verify that disabling one agent credential leaves human sessions and other integrations unaffected.

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: No transactional or compensating logic exists. Both pages issue single standalone <cfquery> SELECT statements with no <cftransaction> wrapper, no saga or two-phase pattern, and no undo operation. download.cfm streams from the local filesystem with deletefile="no". The README notes documents live on local disk "D:\docroot\files (no object storage, no backups offsite)" on a single instance, so there is also no restore path if state is lost. agent_scope resolved to read-only, so the conditional BLOCKER resolves to RISK-SAFETY.
findings.gap: The system has no compensation primitive at all. The read paths present today need none, but the documented upload path writes to a single local disk with no backup, meaning any state damage is unrecoverable rather than compensable.
findings.recommendation: Before any write-enabled integration, wrap multi-step document operations in explicit transactions, move document bytes to durable versioned object storage so a bad write can be rolled back to a prior version, and define an explicit undo operation for upload and delete.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only (has_write_operations=false), so the conditional BLOCKER resolves to its read-only severity.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: No multi-step write workflow is exposed in index.cfm or download.cfm; has_http_rpc_surface is true so the INFO surface calibration does not apply, and the archetype is data-gateway rather than stateless-utility.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: Current state is readable only through the HTML UI. index.cfm renders doc_id, title, category, uploaded_by and uploaded_on into a presentation table, and download.cfm looks up a single filename by doc_id. There is no status query endpoint and no JSON representation of document state; the state must be recovered by parsing markup.
findings.gap: An agent cannot inspect document state in a machine-readable form before acting; it would have to scrape the HTML table, coupling it to presentation markup that carries no contract.
findings.recommendation: Expose the document metadata already selected in index.cfm lines 23-27 as a JSON read endpoint (list and get-by-id) so callers can inspect state without parsing HTML.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting exists at any layer reachable from this repository. There is no IaC (no API Gateway throttle, no WAF rate rule), no middleware, and no application-level counter in index.cfm or download.cfm. Every request to index.cfm executes an unbounded LIKE '%...%' scan against dbo.documents, and every download.cfm request streams a file from local disk on the single Windows instance described in the README.
findings.gap: A looping caller can issue unbounded full-table LIKE scans and unbounded disk reads against a single-instance SQL Server 2005 backend with no throttle, which will degrade or exhaust the server for all users.
findings.recommendation: Place the agent-facing surface behind a gateway enforcing per-principal request throttling, and add a server-side result cap and query timeout so a single caller cannot monopolise the database.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No business-domain limits exist: no per-caller caps on records returned or documents retrieved, no bulk-operation size limit, and no spend threshold. The document listing query in index.cfm has no TOP/row cap, and download.cfm imposes no per-caller retrieval ceiling. agent_scope resolved to read-only, so this is recorded as INFO.
findings.gap: There are no business-impact caps. Under the current read-only scope this limits exposure to mass document retrieval rather than mass mutation, but no ceiling on documents retrieved per caller per session exists.
findings.recommendation: When scope expands to writes, add per-principal business limits (documents retrieved per hour, documents modified or deleted per run) configurable per agent identity and enforced independently of request-rate throttling.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: agent_scope=read-only (has_write_operations=false), so the scope-calibrated RISK downgrades to INFO.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: A read-only caller cannot modify or delete records or trigger spend, so business transaction limits are planning input for future scope expansion.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No non-production environment is defined. The repository contains no environment-specific configuration, no docker-compose file, no seed or synthetic data script, and no IaC. The README describes the sole deployment path as "Copy .cfm files over the network share to wwwroot" on a single Windows EC2 instance, implying changes are exercised directly against production.
findings.gap: There is no environment with production-equivalent data shape in which agent behaviour could be rehearsed, so the first execution of any new integration would be against live documents and the live database.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a staging instance with a restored, de-identified copy of the docportal schema and a representative document set on separate storage, and require integrations to be validated there before production exposure.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A = Yes: the application owns a persistent SQL Server store (datasource "docportal", table dbo.documents) holding internal policy documents and forms plus user-attribution fields (uploaded_by, uploaded_on), and the README describes it as an intranet portal for policy documents and forms. Stage B — B1 is CLEAR: both queries use explicit column projections (index.cfm selects doc_id, title, category, uploaded_by, uploaded_on; download.cfm selects filename only) and no credential or secret column is returned to callers. B2 FIRES: there is no access differentiation whatsoever — a single session-existence check grants every caller the complete document list regardless of category, and download.cfm applies no check at all, so no scope separates sensitive document categories from routine ones. B3 is ABSENT: no classification tags, no field-level sensitivity annotations, no Macie/Presidio integration and no documented classification policy exist anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: No access-control differentiation exists between sensitive and non-sensitive document categories (B2), and no formal classification metadata identifies which documents are sensitive (B3). An agent granted document read access necessarily receives every document in the store, including any HR, legal or financial material filed in it.
findings.recommendation: Classify the document categories already present in the category column, then enforce category-scoped access per caller principal in both the listing predicate and the download handler so an agent identity can be restricted to non-sensitive categories. Record the classification as queryable metadata rather than convention.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only and B1 is clear, but B2 fires at RISK-SAFETY (no access-control differentiation), which sets the overall severity.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: B1 would have been the BLOCKER path only if sensitive fields were returned in general responses under write-enabled scope; here column projections are explicit and scope is read-only, so the highest firing sub-check is B2.

b1.reasoning: CLEAR — explicit column projections in index.cfm (lines 23-27) and download.cfm (line 4); no password, token or credential column is exposed to callers.

b2.reasoning: FIRES — the only access control is structKeyExists(session,'userid') in index.cfm lines 5-7, which grants all documents to all callers; download.cfm has no check, so no scope distinguishes sensitive from non-sensitive data.

b3.reasoning: ABSENT — no classification tags, field annotations, PII detection tooling or documented policy; the category column is free-form convention only.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: The system holds a persistent data store (SQL Server 2005 via the docportal datasource) and document bytes on local disk at D:\docroot\files per the README. No residency or sovereignty controls or statements were found: the repository contains no IaC with region constraints, no cross-region replication configuration, and no GDPR/LGPD/HIPAA references in README.md or either CFML page. agent_scope resolved to read-only, so the conditional BLOCKER resolves to RISK-SAFETY.
findings.gap: The jurisdictional constraints on the document corpus are undocumented, so there is no basis on which to decide whether document contents may be transmitted to an LLM endpoint in another region. Document bodies are streamed verbatim by download.cfm, meaning full file contents — not just metadata — would cross whatever boundary the agent runtime sits behind.
findings.recommendation: Determine and document the residency classification of the document corpus before any agent consumes document bodies, pin the agent runtime and model endpoint to an approved region, and record the constraint alongside the document category classification from DATA-Q1.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only (has_write_operations=false), so the conditional BLOCKER resolves to its read-only severity.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_persistent_data_store is true (SQL Server docportal datasource plus local document storage), so the INFO surface calibration does not apply; read-only access still transmits full document bodies to the agent runtime.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: The document listing query in index.cfm is unbounded: SELECT doc_id, title, category, uploaded_by, uploaded_on FROM documents WHERE title LIKE '%#url.q#%' ORDER BY uploaded_on DESC. There is no TOP clause, no OFFSET/FETCH, no limit or cursor parameter, and no page-size control. The only filter is the single free-text title term; category and uploaded_by are returned but not filterable. With an empty url.q (the <cfparam> default on line 8) the predicate matches every row in the table.
findings.gap: A caller that omits the search term receives the entire documents table in one response. There is no pagination or result cap to bound the payload, and no structured filters to narrow it by category, uploader or date.
findings.recommendation: Add server-enforced pagination (page size with a hard maximum, plus a cursor or OFFSET/FETCH clause) and explicit filter parameters for category, uploaded_by and date range, and return the total count so callers can page deterministically.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: There is no input validation anywhere. index.cfm takes url.q via <cfparam> with no type, length or character constraint and interpolates it directly into the SQL LIKE predicate (line 26), which the file's own comment acknowledges: "SQL built by string concatenation - injection vulnerable". download.cfm interpolates url.id straight into WHERE doc_id = #url.id# (line 4) with no numeric check and no <cfparam>, then concatenates the resulting doc.filename onto D:\docroot\files\ and passes it to <cfcontent file="..."> — a path-traversal exposure the file comments also acknowledge. No <cfqueryparam>, no validation library, no request size limit and no structured validation error responses exist.
findings.gap: Both entry points accept arbitrary input shapes with no validation and interpolate them into SQL and into a filesystem path. Malformed or hostile input is neither rejected nor reported; it reaches the database and the filesystem, and failures surface as ColdFusion error pages with no field-level detail.
findings.recommendation: Bind every query parameter with <cfqueryparam> (cf_sql_integer for url.id, cf_sql_varchar with a maxlength for url.q), validate url.id as a positive integer before use, canonicalise the resolved filepath and reject any path that escapes D:\docroot\files, and return structured validation errors naming the offending field and constraint.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Partial temporal metadata exists. dbo.documents carries uploaded_on, which index.cfm selects and sorts on (ORDER BY uploaded_on DESC) and renders with dateFormat(uploaded_on, 'mm/dd/yyyy') — dropping the time component and any timezone. There is no updated_at or last-modified column, no evidence of UTC normalisation, no Cache-Control or X-Data-Age header, and no consistency or freshness indicator on any response.
findings.gap: Timestamps are upload-time only, rendered date-only with no timezone, and no response metadata signals whether the data returned is current. An agent reasoning about document recency cannot establish ordering within a day or detect staleness.
findings.recommendation: Store and return uploaded_on as a full UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 form (not a localised date string), add a last-modified column maintained on change, and include freshness metadata on responses once the JSON surface exists.

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: No log redaction is possible because no logging layer exists to redact in: there is no <cflog>, no Application.cfc, no log scrubbing middleware, no CloudWatch filter and no Macie integration. Failures instead fall through to default ColdFusion 8 error pages, which render the failing query text and request scope — and since url.q is interpolated into the SQL on index.cfm line 26 and session.fullname is rendered on line 15, user-supplied search terms and user names are present in the data that an unhandled exception page would display. The README confirms the application runs over plain HTTP on the internal network, so that output is also unencrypted in transit.
findings.gap: User search terms and user identities reach error output through an uncontrolled path, with no redaction, no structured logging to apply redaction to, and no control over who sees the resulting error pages.
findings.recommendation: Disable detailed ColdFusion error output in production and add an Application.cfc onError handler that logs a structured record with user-supplied values redacted, then apply an allowlist to the fields written to the access log once logging is introduced (AUTH-Q6).

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: A persistent data store exists but no data-quality instrumentation accompanies it. No profiling report, null-rate monitoring, duplicate detection, freshness SLA or quality dashboard was found in the repository. The documents table has no constraint evidence available here, and because download.cfm resolves files by concatenating doc.filename onto a fixed directory, a row whose filename is stale or whose file is missing from disk fails only at stream time.
findings.gap: There is no measure of completeness or correctness for the document corpus, and no detection of rows whose underlying file is missing — an agent cannot distinguish a genuinely absent document from a broken reference.
findings.recommendation: Profile dbo.documents for null and duplicate rates on title, category and filename, and add a reconciliation job that reports rows whose filename does not resolve to a file on disk.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: Neither the schema nor the interface is versioned. There are no database migration files, no JSON Schema/Avro/Protobuf definitions, no schema registry and no OpenAPI definitions. The page URLs carry no version segment (index.cfm, download.cfm?id=) and no Accept-Version handling exists. There is no changelog or deprecation notice; the only version marker in the repository is the cosmetic footer string "ACME Document Portal v2.3" in index.cfm line 45, and the header comment records the file was "Built 2007, last edited 2016". No CI configuration exists, so no breaking-change detection runs.
findings.gap: The documents schema and the page contract can both change with no version signal and no detection, so any agent tool binding would break silently and without warning.
findings.recommendation: Bring the docportal schema under migration control, version the new API surface in its path, and add breaking-change detection (OpenAPI diff on the spec, plus migration review) to a CI pipeline.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: The exposed field names are readable and self-describing: doc_id, title, category, uploaded_by, uploaded_on and filename (index.cfm lines 23-27, download.cfm line 4). They use full words in snake_case rather than legacy abbreviation codes, so no data dictionary is needed to interpret them. The one ambiguity is category, whose permitted values are not enumerated anywhere in the repository, and uploaded_by, whose type (user id versus display name) is not declared.
findings.gap: Field naming is adequate for LLM reasoning. What is missing is the value domain: the set of valid category values and the identity format of uploaded_by are undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Document the permitted category values and the identity format of uploaded_by as part of the schema description, so an agent can construct valid category filters without sampling the data.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No catalog or metadata layer exists. No Glue Data Catalog, DataHub, Collibra or Alation reference, no data dictionary file and no schema documentation were found. The only description of what the system holds is the prose in README.md ("Legacy intranet portal for sharing policy documents and forms"); the dbo.documents column set must be inferred from the SELECT lists in index.cfm and download.cfm.
findings.gap: There is no discoverable description of the document corpus or its schema, so teams building agent tools against this system must reverse-engineer the data model from the two CFML pages.
findings.recommendation: Publish a schema description for dbo.documents and the document store — column meanings, category value domain and ownership — in a catalog or at minimum a versioned schema document in the repository.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: Neither tracing nor structured logging is present. No OpenTelemetry or X-Ray instrumentation exists, no traceparent or correlation header is read or propagated, and no request_id or correlation_id is generated. Neither index.cfm nor download.cfm emits a log line of any kind — there is no <cflog>, no Application.cfc and no logging configuration in the repository. The only diagnostics available are IIS and ColdFusion server logs outside this repository.
findings.gap: There is no correlation identifier and no application log, so a failed request cannot be reconstructed. An agent-initiated failure would be indistinguishable from any other request in the server logs.
findings.recommendation: Add an Application.cfc that accepts or generates a correlation id per request, propagates it to responses, and writes structured JSON log entries for each search and download including the correlation id, principal and outcome.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting is configured. The repository contains no IaC and therefore no CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no SLO definitions and no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration; there are no health or readiness endpoints in either page to alert on. The README notes the design is a "Single instance; reboot = downtime", with no monitoring described.
findings.gap: Error-rate and latency degradation on the document pages is undetected, so an overload or outage would be discovered only when users or callers report it.
findings.recommendation: Add a health endpoint and define alarms on error rate and latency percentiles for the agent-facing surface, routed to an on-call destination, before exposing the system to automated callers.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: No infrastructure is defined as code. Searched for *.tf/*.tfvars, CloudFormation templates, CDK entry points, Helm charts, Kustomize overlays and Ansible playbooks — none exist; the repository holds only README.md, index.cfm, download.cfm and .gitignore. The integration surface is therefore configured by hand: IIS 7 and the ColdFusion Administrator datasource are managed through consoles per the README, and deployment is "Copy .cfm files over the network share to wwwroot". None of the three required sub-checks pass — no IaC definition, no automated plan or peer review of infrastructure change, and no drift detection.
findings.gap: The server, the datasource credential and the network exposure are all manually managed with no reviewable definition and no drift detection, so the configuration an agent would depend on is neither reproducible nor auditable.
findings.recommendation: Define the agent-facing surface as code — the compute, the gateway, the IAM/identity configuration and the secret — under pull-request review, and enable drift detection against those definitions.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No pipeline exists. Searched for .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml and appspec.yml — none are present. Deployment is manual file copy to wwwroot over a network share per the README, so there is no build, no automated test stage, and no contract or breaking-change check between a change and production.
findings.gap: Changes reach production without any automated verification, so a modification that breaks the integration surface (for example renaming a column in the index.cfm SELECT list) is caught only in production.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a pipeline that builds, tests and deploys the application, and add contract validation of the agent-facing API — spec validation plus a breaking-change diff — as a gate before deployment.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No rollback mechanism exists. There is no blue/green or canary configuration, no CodeDeploy or Helm release management, and no feature flags. Deployment is an in-place file copy to wwwroot on a single instance, so reverting means manually copying the previous .cfm files back — and the README notes the instance is a single point of failure ("reboot = downtime, disk loss = data loss"). No deployment artifact or release version is retained; the last recorded edit to index.cfm was 2016.
findings.gap: Recovery from a bad change depends on a manual file copy with no retained known-good artifact and no automated revert path, so the 15-30 minute recovery target cannot be relied on.
findings.recommendation: Deploy versioned, immutable artifacts to at least two instances behind a load balancer with an automated revert to the previous version, and rehearse the rollback so the recovery time is measured rather than assumed.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There are no tests of any kind. The repository contains no test directory, no test files, no Postman/Newman collection and no test framework dependency (there is no dependency manifest at all). Neither index.cfm nor download.cfm has any accompanying test for input handling, output format, error responses or edge cases such as a non-numeric url.id or a filename that does not resolve on disk.
findings.gap: The behaviour of the two entry points is entirely unverified, so no change can be shown not to alter the contract a caller depends on.
findings.recommendation: Add automated tests for the document search and download operations covering valid input, invalid and missing id values, empty search terms, and the missing-file case, and run them in the pipeline introduced for ENG-Q2.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption at rest is configured or evidenced. The README places document bytes on a local Windows disk at D:\docroot\files with "no object storage, no backups offsite", and metadata in SQL Server 2005 — a version that predates SQL Server's modern encryption defaults and reached end of support in April 2016. There is no IaC, so no kms_key_id, no customer-managed key and no EBS or database encryption setting exists anywhere in the repository. The README also records that traffic runs over plain HTTP with no TLS, so the data is unprotected in transit as well.
findings.gap: Document contents and metadata are stored unencrypted on a single instance with no key management, so loss or theft of the disk exposes the entire corpus an agent would be able to read.
findings.recommendation: Move document bytes to encrypted object storage with a customer-managed KMS key, enable encryption at rest on the database volume as part of the platform upgrade off SQL Server 2005, and terminate TLS in front of the application.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no operation exceeding 30s and no long-running workflow exists. index.cfm runs a single SELECT and download.cfm streams one file synchronously; no background job framework, queue worker or job-status pattern is present in the repository.

evaluations.title: Event Emission for State Changes
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — the detected archetype is data-gateway, not stateful-crud or orchestrator, and the repository contains no state-change path that could emit events (both queries are SELECTs).

evaluations.title: Concurrency Controls
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — the trigger requires agent_scope=write-enabled, and scope resolved to read-only (has_write_operations=false).

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — the service has no external dependency calls. Its only outbound dependency is the SQL Server docportal datasource; no <cfhttp>, HTTP client or downstream service call appears in index.cfm or download.cfm.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no priority was supplied in additionalPlanContext and the repository provides no evidence of critical-path status (README describes an internal intranet portal for policy documents).

evaluations.title: Draft/Pending State
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — the trigger requires agent_scope=write-enabled, and scope resolved to read-only (has_write_operations=false).

evaluations.title: Configurable Approval Gates
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — the trigger requires agent_scope=write-enabled, and scope resolved to read-only (has_write_operations=false).

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: Informational-absence suppression: the system emits no metrics or telemetry of any kind (no put_metric_data, no dashboard, no custom metric emission in index.cfm or download.cfm, and no observability configuration in the repository), so there is no observability surface to assess and no actionable informational signal to report.

items.summary: Establish a programmatic API surface and machine identity for it, then close the safety gaps that depend on having an attributable principal: scoped and action-level authorization, credential rotation, audit logging, revocation, rate limiting and data-access differentiation.

Harden the surface and the platform around it: input validation and parameterised queries, pagination, structured errors, schema and contract versioning, observability, CI/CD with rollback, IaC governance, staging and encryption at rest.

Round out machine-consumability and documentation: JSON response format, rate-limit headers, data-quality reconciliation, schema/catalog documentation and the idempotency design for the future upload path.

recommended_actions.action: Expose document search and retrieval as a versioned JSON API
recommended_actions.rationale: There is no programmatic interface today — integration would require scraping HTML from index.cfm or querying SQL Server directly, bypassing the session gate. A documented JSON API is the prerequisite for every other control.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce machine identity with per-agent credentials and enforce it on every path
recommended_actions.rationale: Authentication is human-session only and download.cfm has no check at all, so no caller can be attributed or revoked. Identity must land before authorization, audit and data scoping can mean anything.

recommended_actions.action: Add scoped, action-level authorization and category-based data access control
recommended_actions.rationale: A single session-existence check grants every caller the whole document corpus, so a read-only agent cannot be constrained to a document subset or to read operations.

recommended_actions.action: Rotate the disclosed ColdFusion Administrator credential and move secrets to a managed store
recommended_actions.rationale: README.md discloses the administrator password in plaintext with no rotation, making it readable by anyone with repository access.

recommended_actions.action: Parameterise all queries and validate inputs at the boundary
recommended_actions.rationale: url.q and url.id are interpolated directly into SQL and into a filesystem path, and the listing query is unbounded — the code comments acknowledge both the injection and path-traversal exposure.

recommended_actions.action: Add audit logging, correlation ids and alerting for the agent-facing surface
recommended_actions.rationale: No log line is written by either page, so agent-initiated document retrievals would be untraceable and degradation undetected.

recommended_actions.action: Enforce request throttling and business-impact caps on the agent-facing surface
recommended_actions.rationale: An unbounded LIKE scan with no throttle on a single SQL Server 2005 instance means a looping caller can degrade the system for all users.

recommended_actions.action: Define the integration surface as code with CI/CD, rollback, staging and encryption at rest
recommended_actions.rationale: Deployment is a manual file copy to a single unencrypted instance with no tests, no rollback path and no staging environment, so the surface an agent depends on is neither reproducible nor recoverable.
